summary: Sampling-proxy heartbeat fanout causing cross-tenant GPU credit bleed and delayed autoscale recovery
description: Issue summary: During the ap-northeast dedicated window on 2026-03-10 we observed a persistent throughput degradation for customer NimbusAI. P50 remained stable but p99 token latency increased ~3x and aggregate tokens/sec dropped ~28% for a 45 minute window. Impact: customer-facing production jobs experienced elevated response-time and backpressure, triggering retries and partial user-facing failures. Hypothesis: short-lived control connections (sampling heartbeats) from an internal sampling-proxy sidecar saturated allocator credit accounting and induced autoscaler shrink decisions, leading to transient GPU credit scarcity and slow recovery.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Recreate in ap-northeast dedicated pool with NimbusAI traffic profile (mix of short chatlets and embeddings).
2) Deploy sampling-proxy with increased heartbeat_concurrency=120 (recently rolled).
3) Observe sidecar connection churn metrics and allocator-credit-available metrics while running steady microburst traffic.
4) Watch autoscaler activity: pre-scale down credit dip followed by scale decision and delayed spin-up due to cooldown window.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:15:20Z [autoscaler] decision: shrink by 2 replicas due to credit threshold breach; cooldown_timer set 300s
2026-03-10T09:54:00Z [telemetry] p99_token_latency increased from 320ms -> 1.1s concurrent with reduced attach_rate
investigation_notes: Initial triage: not a model kernel regression; CPU and GPU util remained moderate, but attach/slot allocation rate fell sharply.
Correlation found between sampling-proxy rollout at 09:12 and sudden short-lived connection spike; sidecar telemetry shows aggressive heartbeat fanout across tenants.

Allocator accounting treats short-lived connections as slot reservations until connection teardown; high fanout created transient reservation pressure that autoscaler interpreted as sustained demand drop and reclaimed capacity.

Observed autoscaler hysteresis: when capacity was reclaimed, reclaimed GPUs remained offline for cooldown window preventing rapid re-attach even after connections dropped, amplifying throughput impact.
Cross-tenant effect: other tenants in the same reserved pool experienced degraded attach rates resulting in perceived noisy-neighbor symptoms.
SRE note: internal sampling-proxy change (config increase) pushed without rate-limiting; rollout affected many nodes simultaneously in ap-northeast fleet.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:30 - Support (Elena): Customer reported p99 spikes; escalated to SRE. Added to incident channel #incidents-dedicated-ap-northeast.

2026-03-10 09:42 - SRE (Marco): Identified sidecar heartbeats spike. Temporarily disabled sampling-proxy rollout in region; observed partial recovery within 6 minutes for attach rate but autoscaler cooldown sustained reduced capacity.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (NimbusAI Ops): We saw retries and error rate ~2.8% for chat endpoint during window; appreciate quick triage. Requested ETA for full recovery.

2026-03-10 10:45 - SRE (Marco): Applied workaround patch to sidecar config (rate-limit heartbeats + connection pooling). Monitoring shows allocator credits returning to baseline; p99 trending downwards.

2026-03-11 11:20 - Engineering (Priya): Root-cause analysis draft: allocator accounting is overly sensitive to transient short-lived connections — filed runtime PR to add ephemeral-connection hysteresis and to exclude sidecar heartbeat namespace from slot reservations in SR-1623.
2026-03-12 08:14 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of mitigation and planned next steps; flagged for follow-up postmortem and config hardening.
resolution: Workaround implemented: rolled back aggressive sampling-proxy config in ap-northeast and deployed connection-pooling + heartbeat rate-limiter. Autoscaler cooldown parameters temporarily reduced to 120s for affected pools to accelerate recovery. Engineering fix: PR #1623 changes allocator to ignore designated-sidecar namespace heartbeats for slot-reservation accounting and adds a short hysteresis window for ephemeral-connection spikes. Post-incident actions: add canary gating for sidecar config changes, add alert on short_lived_conn_rate > baseline*3, update dedicated-pool runbook with guidance for sidecar rollouts.
postmortem_actions: 1) SR-1623 merged and scheduled for staged rollout (qa -> us-east -> ap-northeast).
2) Create alert: allocator.ephemeral_conn_rate > 3x baseline in 1m -> auto-pause sidecar rollout and page SRE.
3) Runbook update: 'Sidecar Rollout Safety' checklist and mandatory canary size set to 1% of nodes for first 10 minutes.
4) Customer follow-up: compensation credit applied for 45-minute impact window; customer success to confirm acceptance.
